synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the PR solves a real problem (crash logs lost before telemetry setup) with a sound high-level design (buffer early, install OTLP late, replay), but the implementation has structural and correctness issues at every interesting boundary. The most consistent findings across all six reviewers: the OTLP LoggingHandler is rediscovered by isinstance scan in two places instead of being held by reference, the buffer is an unbounded list with no cap or eviction policy, and _shutdown_telemetry mutates the global root logger handler set as a side effect, removing handlers it does not own. The PR also bundles several unrelated changes (makefile parallelism removal, dropped test file, worker.py race-fix reorder, proc_pool process_closed semantic change) that should ship separately. Multiple lifecycle methods overlap around one piece of state, and the crash-path synthesis of a RecordingOptions to drive side effects conflates policy with mechanism. Recommended: capture the OTLP handler reference at install time, bound the buffer with a deque(maxlen=N), scope handler removal to the specific instance installed, and split the unrelated changes into separate commits.

issues.description: OTLP LoggingHandler discovered by isinstance scan in both flush and shutdown paths instead of by captured reference
issues.detail: _flush_early_log_buffer and _shutdown_telemetry both walk logging.getLogger().handlers looking for the first LoggingHandler instance. This is fragile coupling: if a user attaches their own OTLP LoggingHandler, or if _setup_cloud_tracer ever attaches more than one or attaches it elsewhere, behavior breaks silently — wrong handler is flushed, or someone else's handler is removed. _setup_cloud_tracer knows what handler it installed; it should return/stash that reference and the flush and shutdown paths should operate on the explicit instance. This is the same anti-pattern in two places and is the root cause of several other findings.

issues.description: _shutdown_telemetry removes ALL LoggingHandlers from the root logger, not just the one this module installed
issues.detail: The loop walks root.handlers and removes every LoggingHandler instance before force_flush. The deadlock concern is real (logs emitted during export re-enter the handler), but the fix mutates global state owned by other code. If a user or another subsystem installed their own LoggingHandler, it is silently detached as a side effect of telemetry shutdown. The function's stated contract (shut down telemetry providers) does not advertise this postcondition. Track the handler installed by _setup_cloud_tracer by identity and remove only that one.

issues.description: PR bundles multiple unrelated changes that should ship as separate commits
issues.detail: The commit message says 'upload logs on crash' but the diff also: reorders queue_msg vs pending_assignments in worker.py (a real race fix), reworks shutdown flush behavior, emits a new process_closed event from proc_pool on init failure, disables pytest -n auto and drops tests/test_plugin_google_stt.py from the makefile, and adds pythonpath to pyproject. Each has its own failure mode and its own reason to be reverted. Split into separate commits with their own justifications so bisect and review work.

issues.description: _BufferingHandler.buffer is an unbounded list with no cap, eviction policy, or time bound
issues.detail: Every LogRecord is appended to self.buffer with no upper limit. Crash paths are exactly when log volume spikes (tracebacks, retries, chatty libraries), and if session.start() is delayed or the job hangs before crashing, the buffer grows monotonically. LogRecord also retains args, exc_info tracebacks, and frame locals, so this is both a memory and lifetime hazard. Use a collections.deque(maxlen=N) with a documented drop policy so the abstraction's resource behavior is part of its contract.

issues.description: _flush_early_log_buffer silently drops buffered records if no OTLP LoggingHandler is found
issues.detail: The function removes the buffering handler unconditionally, then iterates root.handlers searching for a LoggingHandler. If _setup_cloud_tracer did not actually install one (failure, race, ordering change), the buffer is dropped with no warning, no diagnostic, no retry. This is exactly the failure mode the PR is trying to fix — crash logs being lost — and a silent miss here defeats the purpose. Emit a logger.warning when the OTLP handler is absent so the failure is observable.

issues.description: Makefile silently removes pytest -n auto parallelism and drops tests/test_plugin_google_stt.py with no explanation
issues.detail: The unit-tests target loses -n auto (serializing the suite) and excludes a plugin test file. Neither change is mentioned in the PR description or commented in the diff. If google_stt is flaky or xdist interacts badly, say so in the commit message. As written, this is a quiet reduction in test coverage and CI speed bundled inside a feature PR.

issues.description: Three overlapping lifecycle methods (_start_log_buffering, _stop_log_buffering, _flush_early_log_buffer) for one piece of state
issues.detail: _stop_log_buffering and _flush_early_log_buffer(replay=False) are operationally identical. The control flow across init_recording's early-return branch, _on_cleanup's crash path, and the success path is spread across three entry points where one parameterized function would do. Collapse to a single operation that takes the destination (None = drop, handler = replay-then-drop). The underlying state machine is simple; the API around it is not.

issues.description: _on_cleanup synthesizes a RecordingOptions to trigger handler setup, conflating policy with mechanism
issues.detail: The cleanup path constructs RecordingOptions(audio=False, traces=False, logs=True, transcript=False) and calls init_recording purely as a side effect to install the OTLP handler and flush the buffer. RecordingOptions is a user-facing policy value; using it as a control-flow lever conflates two concerns and hardcodes logs=True regardless of user settings. Extract a small _ensure_otlp_log_handler() helper that both init_recording and the crash path call, so _on_cleanup says what it means.

issues.description: init_recording's early-return now has a hidden side effect: stopping log buffering
issues.detail: Previously 'if already initialized or not cloud: return' was a pure guard. Now it calls self._stop_log_buffering() in the same branch, silently changing the function's contract. Calling init_recording a second time tears down buffering that may have been intended for a later flush. Pull this side effect out into the cleanup/setup path that actually owns the buffer lifecycle, or split into init_recording() and a separate _finalize_log_buffering().

issues.description: Replay path bypasses _log_filter that decorates records with job/session context
issues.detail: _on_setup installs self._log_filter on existing handlers via addFilter so records get job/session attribution. The new _BufferingHandler is added to the root logger without that filter, and on replay the buffered records are pushed directly into the OTLP LoggingHandler via h.emit(record) — bypassing both the filter and Logger.handle(). The records most needing attribution (early crashes) end up uploaded without it. Apply the filter to the buffering handler or route replay through the logging machinery.

issues.description: _on_entry_done forces _shutdown_fut from a done-callback with only InvalidStateError suppressed; precedence and ordering invariants are unstated
issues.detail: The new branch calls set_result on shutdown_fut from a done-callback whenever the job task raises. contextlib.suppress(asyncio.InvalidStateError) handles the already-set case, but there's no stated invariant about when shutdown_fut may legitimately already be in another terminal state, nor about precedence between this callback and the normal user-initiated shutdown path. The synthesized _ShutdownInfo also discards the actual exception, using a constant 'job crashed' string. Carry the exception (or its repr) in ShutdownInfo and document the ordering contract explicitly.

issues.description: process_closed event semantics broadened to include init-failure cases without documentation
issues.detail: proc_pool now emits process_closed when initialization fails, in addition to the existing close paths. The test diff confirms this: 'if proc.pid is not None: pids.append(proc.pid)' had to be added because uninitialized processes have no pid. Any existing listener that assumed process_closed implies 'process previously initialized / had a pid' is now silently broken. Either rename the new emission (process_init_failed) or document the contract change at the emit site.

issues.description: _on_cleanup catches bare Exception around init_recording; buffer-leak path on partial failure not reasoned about
issues.detail: If init_recording raises after _recording_initialized is set to True but before _flush_early_log_buffer runs, the buffer may remain attached and records are lost. The cleanup invariant ('after _on_cleanup returns, _early_log_handler is detached') is preserved only by the except branch. Ensure _stop_log_buffering runs in a finally, not just on exception, and state the cleanup invariant explicitly.

issues.description: worker.py reorder of _queue_msg and pending_assignments registration is an unexplained race fix bundled in
issues.detail: Registering wait_assignment in _pending_assignments before awaiting _queue_msg(availability_resp) looks like a real fix for a race where the server could send the assignment before the future is registered. But it's buried in a log-upload PR with no commit message. If it is a race fix, it deserves its own commit and its own test.

issues.description: Lazy import of RecordingOptions inside _on_cleanup hides a module-load-order assumption
issues.detail: _on_cleanup performs 'from .voice.agent_session import RecordingOptions' inline. This is presumably to dodge a circular import, but the constraint isn't stated. A lazy import buried in an error path is a classic way for an ImportError to only manifest in production crash handling. Add a one-line comment explaining the cycle, or — better — thread the OTLP handler reference explicitly so the inline import isn't needed.

issues.description: _BufferingHandler exposes its mutable internal buffer as a public attribute
issues.detail: self.buffer is a public mutable list with no encapsulation; callers in job.py iterate handler.buffer directly. The invariant 'records are only appended in emit order, never mutated externally' is not enforced. Give the handler a drain() or replay(target_handler) method that hides the list and keeps the OTLP-handler knowledge inside traces.py.

issues.description: Local 'from opentelemetry.sdk._logs import LoggingHandler' uses a private OTel module path
issues.detail: The underscore in sdk._logs marks the module as not part of the public OTel API. Coupling correctness of crash-log delivery to a private import is fragile across OTel versions. Pin the dependency with a comment stating the version contract, or route through a public surface.

issues.description: test_ipc retry assertion changed from 'retry succeeds' to 'retry also times out' with weak justification
issues.detail: tests/test_ipc.py previously asserted that after initialization failure warmup should be retried successfully. The new version waits for both start_q and close_q, asserting that the retry batch also times out. The comment states the new observed behavior but not the invariant being protected — does the pool retry indefinitely? back off? A reader cannot tell whether this test passes because of the fix or because of an unrelated change in retry semantics.
